correctness.rationale: A disjoint and unique factorization of each commuting partial injection gives C. Directed-cycle inspection makes nilpotence equivalent to both an acyclic chain-index factor and a cycle-free residual matching on its s shared vertices. The number of acyclic partial injections is \(r!/(r-k)!\) times binomial(r-1,k), including r=0. Marked-cycle inclusion exclusion gives inner signed cycle enumerator 1,-1,0 for j=0,1,>=2, proving \(H_{m,s}(t)=P_m(t)-stP_{m-1}(t)\). Degrees and leading coefficients follow. An independent direct functional-digraph/multiplication checker validated all ranks for every (r,s) with 1<=2r+s<=6 (15 cases), including both degenerate boundaries.

value.rationale: The two-parameter family of prescribed square-zero centralizers is a canonical representation-theoretic/combinatorial slice of finite symmetric inverse monoids. Full nilpotent-by-rank enumeration requires combining distinct centralizer and acyclic-chain constraints. The marked-cycle sieve gives a compact cancellation of all overlaps of size >=2, and the top nilpotent rank equals the number of centralizer units \(r!s!\). The results apply in infinitely many sizes and classify all ranks, not an arbitrary finite table.
